ops.body: Fixed by the v12 lexicon redesign (b2d2b552, feat!(sentiment): surface-only lexicon lookup). The task's own hunch ("surface-form lookup before lemma, like afinn itself") was the answer taken to its conclusion: both lemmatizers are deleted and lookup is surface-only against shared package-data TSVs, so 'this is broken' hits DOMAIN_OVERRIDES['broken']=-3 deterministically on both backends — the 'break'=-2 vs 'broken'=-3 calibration distinction is preserved and now reliably reachable. The criterion's first branch holds: tests/test_lexicon_parity.py pins "this is broken" as an exact-equality floor-3 hostile hit on Python AND Rust (45/45 hermetic, no models). The audit that gated the change measured 23% cross-backend has_hit nondeterminism under the old lemma path — all eliminated. Also fixed en passant: 'lost'/'losing' scored 0 on both backends (lemma 'lose' absent from AFINN); they now hit their surface rows at -3.
